column3: “Men, brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”
When they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they became even more quiet. And he said,

“I am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the strictness of the ancestral law, being a zealot for God just as all of you are today.
I persecuted this Way as far as death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women,

as even the high priest and all the council of elders can testify about me. From them I also received letters to the brothers and was traveling to Damascus to bring those who were there bound to Jerusalem so that they might be punished.
“But it happened as I was traveling and drawing near to Damascus, about midday, that suddenly a great light from heaven flashed around me.
And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.’
Now those who were with me saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me.
And I said, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ And the Lord said to me, ‘Get up and go into Damascus, and there it will be told you about all the things that have been appointed for you to do.’
And since I could not see because of the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me and came into Damascus.
Now a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living there,
came to me and stood by me and said to me, ‘Brother Saul, see again!’ And at that very hour I looked up at him.
And he said, ‘The God of our fathers appointed you beforehand to know his will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth,
because you will be a witness for him to all people of the things you have seen and heard.
And now why do you delay? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on his name.’
“And it happened when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple that I fell into a trance
and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and go quickly out of Jerusalem, because they will not accept your testimony about me.’
And I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that in every synagogue I was imprisoning and beating those who believe in you.
And when the blood of Stephen your witness was being poured out, I myself was standing by and approving and guarding the garments of those killing him.’
And he said to me, ‘Go, because I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”
They listened to him as far as this word, and then they raised their voice, saying, “Away from the earth with such a man! For it was not fitting for him to live.”
And as they were crying out and throwing off their garments and tossing dust into the air,
the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined by flogging, so that he might know for what reason they were shouting this way against him.
But when they stretched him out with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman man who has not been condemned?”
When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it, saying, “What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman.”
So the commander came and said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
The commander answered, “I acquired this citizenship with a large sum of money.” Paul said, “But I was even born a citizen.”
Therefore those who were about to examine him immediately withdrew from him, and the commander also became afraid when he learned that he was a Roman and that he had bound him.

But on the next day, wanting to know with certainty why he was being accused by the Jews, he released him and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together. And bringing Paul down, he stood him before them.
